findings.issue: The bounded-deviation note (written by the implementer) is inaccurate. The old regex `^[0-9a-fA-F:.]{2,45}$` already rejected `1` (shorter than 2) and over-long entries (longer than 45), so those are not deviations; only `127.1`-style loose literals are. The note also leaves out two real key changes: (1) `ip:port` entries such as `1.2.3.4:80` used to become key `ip:1.2.3.4:80`; the port is now stripped, so per-port buckets merge. (2) Bracketed v6 `[2001:db8::1]:443` used to fall back to the peer; it now resolves to the address. The contract test case 'loose 1 falls back to peer' is likewise labelled as a deviation when it is unchanged behaviour. The ADR also stays at Status 'Proposed' although the class-L design was accepted. Editing the ADR was an implementer task in T6, but the wording needs a non-author check.
findings.fix: Rewrite the Consequences bullet: canonicalisation (mapped v4, v6 case/full form), `ip:port` port stripped (buckets merge), bracketed v6 now parsed, `127.1`-style shorthand falls back to the peer. Remove `1` and over-long from the list. Carry the same text into the PR description (condition 2). Have the CEO/architect, not the implementer, update Status if the Owner has approved.

findings.issue: AC-10(c) and the assumeTrue: acceptable for this checkpoint, because verify-slice1.md records 1 run and 0 skipped in the docker build, and the skip message is explicit. Two weaknesses remain. (1) If CI ever moves to a host without a 127/8 loopback (macOS runners, some containers), the test skips again and nothing fails, because the verify note only covers this one run. (2) The named fallback, ClientIpPropagationGatewayFilterTest#headerIsTheRequestPeer, is tautological: it feeds a MockServerHttpRequest whose remoteAddress is 127.0.0.2, so it cannot detect the failure AC-10(c) targets (a forwarded-headers strategy or proxy hop changing what the gateway sees as its peer). It is not truly 'equivalent'.
findings.fix: Make the skip fail in CI, e.g. `if (System.getenv("CI") != null) fail(...)`, else assume. Or have the gradle wrapper or verify step grep the JUnit XML for a skipped `downstreamSeesTheRealPeer` and fail. Reword the fallback comment so it does not claim equivalence.

summary: The production change is correct and minimal. GatewayClientIp holds the N-hop rule. RateLimitWebFilter and ClientIpPropagationGatewayFilter both call it and format through ClientAddress.format, so the rate-limit key and the propagated header cannot drift apart. The header is `set` only in a GlobalFilter at order 1, after the -300 x-internal-* strip, so 401/403/429 and no-route requests never carry it, and an unresolvable peer removes the header instead of sending a blank one. ClientAddress.parse uses JDK InetAddress.ofLiteral (no DNS), caps input at 64 chars and never throws. The tests would fail if the rule broke. The contract test runs the real RateLimitWebFilter and the real propagation filter over the AC-1/2 matrix, including null and unresolved peers and the canonicalisation and loose-literal deviations. The integration test goes through real Netty and the real filter chain to an echo stub, covering spoofed XFF; spoofed headers in mixed case, repeated and comma-joined; public, auth and authenticated routes; and the no-forwarding check for 401/403/404/429. AC-10(c) actually ran, with 0 skipped recorded. The assumeTrue is acceptable for now, but a future skip would go unnoticed and its unit fallback is tautological. Two process gates block approval. First, forge-verify --changed was never run, so AC-13 and CTO condition 5 are unmet. Second, the slice is about 906 changed lines against CTO condition 1's 600-line cap on all lines, and verify-slice1.md misreports this as a production-only count. The implementer's ADR deviation note also needs correcting: `1` and over-long entries were already rejected by the old regex, and the `ip:port` key merge and the bracketed-v6 change are not mentioned. Fix both majors (run forge-verify and record its output; split or trim the slice, or get a recorded waiver) and re-request review at the new SHA.
